findings.claim: In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId (credential.id) as its third argument, which is userId. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong calcomUserId.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:53,62,85-94, biginAuth extracts credential.id into credentialId and refreshAccessToken passes credentialId as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens. Because packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,11 expects userId as its third parameter and posts it as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, the sync endpoint receives the credential ID instead of credential.userId.

findings.claim: The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison.

verifier.reason: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-27, the newly added webhook handler compares the incoming header value directly against process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using !== rather than a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual.

findings.claim: parseRefreshTokenResponse sets a missing refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token'. Callers such as office365calendar and Zoom then persist it over the real stored refresh token.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever `refresh_token` is falsy or omitted (which is allowed by `refreshTokenResponseSchema` at packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:56 and by `minimumTokenResponseSchema`). Callers then overwrite and persist it over the real stored refresh token via `prisma.credential.update` in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-272 and packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:104,120-124.

findings.claim: googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts stores the entire parseRefreshTokenResponse safeParse wrapper ({success, data, ...}) as Credential.key instead of its .data. The next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) then throws.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:16-29, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse wrapper ({ success: true, data }), and packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 stores that entire object directly into prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } }) instead of key.data. On the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 throws because the required token fields are nested under data rather than at the top level.

findings.claim: The credential's invalid flag is never reset when the credential is updated.

verifier.reason: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73-80, updating an existing credential only writes `data: { key: keys }` and never resets `invalid: false` (nor do the token-refresh updates such as packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:98-101 or packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96-99). Once a credential is marked `invalid: true` (e.g., packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:112-117), it stays invalid even after new keys are synced via the webhook, causing packages/core/getCalendarsEvents.ts:17 to keep skipping it and the UI to keep flagging it as invalid.

findings.claim: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on parse failure and never returns success: false. The !success branches in Salesforce getClient and Zoom are therefore dead code.

verifier.reason: parseRefreshTokenResponse in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23 throws an Error whenever !refreshTokenResponse.success and therefore only ever returns a result with success: true. Consequently, the !accessTokenParsed.success check in packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94 and the !parsedToken.success check in packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:108-110 are unreachable dead code.
